title: Jester
name: Sarmenti
description: The Jester is a musician who was made a fool of once, and has worn the motley ever since. He treats everything as a joke, his own life included, and laughs as readily in a fight as over a drink, but he cannot stand being the one laughed at. The only great song he ever played ended in a slaughter, and bloodshed has been his muse since. He is poor yet kind and generous to the destitute, and arrives at the Estate because it pays and he does not much care whether he lives.
history: The Jester was a street musician in a city of Loess, busking without ambition until a violinist in a cemetery taught him a melody that woke it. He won a place at the king's court, where for a few years he played at its lesser occasions. When he was finally called to a great feast, it was as the fool: dressed in motley and humiliated while the nobles dined. He played the violinist's song, and under it he butchered the king and the whole court with dirk and sickle. With the hall empty, he cut off his own index finger so he could never play it again.
summary: A sardonic, masked Jester, a court musician turned fool who butchered a king's court under a song he can no longer play.

appearance.features: Missing the index finger of his left hand; face hidden by his mask

clothing.head: Patched red hood, and a mouthless white mask with black diamonds at the eyes
clothing.body: Red motley cowl with gold zigzag trim hung with bells, over a dark tunic
clothing.legs: Dark patched hose, and pointed shoes with a bell at each toe
clothing.accessories: Red gloves, wide buckled belt, lute slung on his back

notes: Speaks like a busker who spent years at court: street talk and dropped g's ('ain't', 'lemme', 'you lot') mixed with courtly words ('twould', 'louche', 'volte-face')
Speaks in terms of music and the stage (tempo, tuning, solos, adagio, crescendo)
Chuckles a low 'heh heh' at small things and laughs out loud in high moments. Under strain it becomes shrill, unhinged laughter that can turn to weeping
Composes aloud, trying half-finished verses about recent events on whoever is near to see how they land
Reacts badly to being mocked or laughed at: he goes cold, turns spiteful, and holds the grudge
Glad to play for anyone, common folk most of all, but sighs and sours when asked to caper or cheer someone up on demand
Talks freely and sourly about his years at court. Asked how he left it, he tells the truth as a joke, with a chuckle, in a way that is hard to take seriously
